passage: Rain drummed on the tin roof, so break was indoors and the classroom was loud and cramped. The teacher held up Nitin's drawing of a boat. "Lovely work, Nitin." Hafsa frowned across the desks. "You are not that good." Nitin's smile slipped. His stomach felt twisty and his eyes stung, and the rain and shouting made it harder to think. He did not brag or snap back. He said, "I like your drawing too, Hafsa," and picked up his crayons.

qa.a: The rain drummed on the tin roof, so break was indoors.

qa.q: What was Nitin feeling when his smile slipped after Hafsa's remark?
qa.a: He felt puzzled and hurt, with a twisty stomach, since he had just been praised and then criticised.

qa.q: What did Nitin do that stayed kind without bragging?
qa.a: He did not brag or snap back, but told Hafsa he liked Hafsa's drawing too. That left the moment calm.

qa.q: What might Hafsa be feeling when she frowned and said "You are not that good"?
qa.a: Hafsa may be feeling envy, wishing to have been praised too. It is Hafsa's feeling, not proof that Nitin did wrong.

grounding: After the teacher praises me, a classmate frowns and says I am not that good; I stay kind and do not brag.

Monday. The teacher praised Yamini's drawing. Harsha frowned. "You're not that good."

Yamini, five, felt puzzled and a bit down. She didn't brag.

Tuesday. Harsha said it again. Yamini's mother said, "Maybe Harsha wishes she got praised too."

Friday. Yamini said, "Harsha, your elephant is nice." Harsha smiled for the first time all week.

qa.q: What did the teacher praise on Monday?
What was Yamini feeling when Harsha said "You're not that good"?
qa.a: Yamini felt puzzled and a bit sad, unsure what she had done wrong.

qa.q: Why was Yamini's choice on Friday a kind one?
qa.a: She stayed kind and didn't brag, understanding Harsha's frown as envy, not proof she did wrong.

qa.q: How might Harsha have felt when the teacher praised Yamini?
qa.a: Harsha probably felt envious and left out.

grounding: Shows a young child confused by a classmate's envious remark after praise, staying kind and not bragging.

The school hall was noisy with the fan broken. The teacher held up Mohit's clay pot. "Beautiful work, Mohit!"

Yogesh muttered, "It's not even round."

Mohit, six, felt his smile wobble. Was it bad?

He looked at the pot, then at Yogesh's empty hands. He didn't boast. He said, "Want to make one together tomorrow?"

Yogesh shrugged, but nodded.

qa.q: What did the teacher hold up?
qa.a: The teacher held up Mohit's clay pot.

qa.q: What was Mohit feeling when his smile wobbled?
qa.a: Mohit felt confused and a little sad, unsure if his pot was bad.

qa.q: What did Mohit do that was wise?
qa.a: He stayed kind and didn't brag, inviting Yogesh to make a pot together.

qa.q: How might Yogesh feel when the teacher praises Mohit?
qa.a: Yogesh likely feels envious and left out.

grounding: Shows a young child hurt by a classmate's envious comment after praise, staying kind and not bragging.
